why_points: The pick: Receptions higher 2.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 3.5, moved to this line) is 79%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 4. This is the best number for the higher side.
Game log, most recent first: 3, 5, 3, 3, 1, 3. Weighted average 3.2; went higher than 2.5 in 5 of 6 games (88% recency-weighted).
Trending up: last 3 games average 3.7 vs 2.3 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±1.1, so the line is 0.6 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): +7% on his average.
PFF: DAL plays man on 28% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 25%); he gains 0.88 yds/route vs man and 1.02 vs zone → -0% from scheme.
PFF: DAL allows 1.85 yds/route to WRs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.57) → +15% against his usual opponents.

PFF: He runs 65% of his routes from the slot (0.83 yds/route there, 0.97 outside); DAL allows 1.83 yds/route to slot WRs and 1.71 outside (league 1.47 / 1.63, opponent-adjusted) → +16% vs his usual opponents.
Projection: we expect 3.1 catches on average; in a typical game 2.8 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 0.3 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 66% and the matchup 63%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 77%, matchup 76%.
Bottom line: we give it 76% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: +20.2 points; that works out to about +36¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
Risks: low line - one play can decide it.
